title: Graded shedding controller and shadowed fallback broker
creator: Aisha Gupta
description:
Goal: Implement a production-safe "graded shedding controller" (GSC) that computes a per-entity (tenant / model / external dependency) degradation score and applies proportionate mitigation (throttles, queues, partial routing) plus a 'shadowed fallback broker' that evaluates and records fallback effectiveness without immediately switching traffic. The feature must support multi-region awareness and be configurable via runtime policies and the Console.

Scope:
- Compute degradation_score = weighted( p99_latency, recent_error_rate, queue_depth, token_cost, capacity_utilization ) per entity.
- Define deterministic policies that map score ranges to mitigation actions (soft-rate-limit, route-to-compatible-variant, response-cache-serving, reject-fast with metadata).
- Shadowed fallback broker: when a mitigation would route to fallback paths (lower-capacity model, cached response), the system also shadow-invokes fallback in parallel to collect quality signals before making fallback live.
- Plumb metrics & traces into Console: per-entity SLO delta, mitigation incidents, fallback quality delta (KL divergence / perplexity delta), and cost delta.

Non-Goals: full rollout automation for all tenants (handled later by Dedicated rollout), complex ML-based threshold tuning (MVP uses heuristics + simple smoothing).
acceptance_criteria: GSC exports a per-entity degradation_score every 10s and surfaces it in Console and logs
Three mitigation levels implemented: light (10% shed), medium (50% shed + route to cheap quantized model), heavy (reject-fast + serve cache)
Shadowed broker collects fallback_quality metrics for every fallback candidate and stores them for 7d
Fallback does not go live for an entity until shadowed broker shows fallback_quality delta < 10% on at least 3 independent windows
Automated canary: enable for 5 internal tenants for 48h, no severe SLO regressions, then expand to a beta cohort
updates: 2026-02-20: Ticket created after SRE on-call postmortem indicated recurring tenant-level latency spikes with unsafe fallbacks.
2026-02-24: Design sync with Runtime and Console teams; agreed on score composition and 3 mitigation levels. Linked design doc.
2026-03-02: PoC of score calculator merged to feature branch; basic metrics emitted to staging. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1849
2026-03-05: Spike showed that naive fallback switch caused 12% quality regression on billing queries; added shadowed broker idea.
2026-03-09: Integration test harness for shadowed broker added; running nightly against synthetic traces. Adjusted default weights (p99:0.5, error_rate:0.3, queue:0.15, cost:0.05).
decisions: Use a weighted linear score for MVP rather than ML-driven classifier to simplify rollout and explainability.
Three mitigation tiers chosen to balance fine-grained control vs configuration surface area.
Shadowed broker will be default-off for customer tenants and enabled during canary/beta to avoid accidental impact.
Fallback readiness gate: require 3 rolling windows with fallback_quality delta <= 10% before switching live traffic.
review_feedback: PM (Tomás Rivera): prefer exposing 'regret' and 'cost' metrics to Console so customers can decide opt-in policies.
Design (Emily Chen): add UI affordance to explain why a tenant is being shed and which mitigation tier is active.
Security (Priya Rao): confirm GDPR-safe handling for shadowed requests; strip user identifiers in shadow path. Added checklist item.
SRE (Liam O'Connor): recommend conservative default thresholds and automatic rollback hooks tied to global SLO regression alarms.
test_plan: Unit tests for score computation with synthetic latency/error traces
Integration tests: simulate tenant blast (burst to p99>1200ms) and assert mitigation level transitions and no hard fallbacks without shadow confirmation
Chaos test: kill regional model pool and assert multi-region routing + canary rollback engages
Quality test: run PTA (production traffic analyzer) to measure fallback_quality delta over shadowed invocations
Load test: verify 95th percentile decision latency for score calc < 15ms under 50k req/s
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): enable GSC and shadowed broker for internal tenants only (3 teams) - 1 week
Phase 1 (canary): enable for 5 low-risk customers and run 48h smoke + 7d analysis
Phase 2 (beta): enable for a beta cohort (50 customers) with Console opt-in and guardrails
Phase 3 (GA): enable with safe defaults; console exposes policy override for enterprise tenants
Rollbacks: automatic disable if global SLO delta > 0.3% or any tenant sees > 5% quality loss within 1h
metrics: fallback_quality_delta: KL / perplexity / heuristics comparing primary vs fallback
SLO impact: global token-p99 and error_rate change pre/post mitigation
cost_delta: estimated per-token cost delta before/after mitigation
risks_mitigations: Risk: Incorrect weight tuning causes over-shedding. Mitigation: conservative defaults + 'regret' metric + human-in-the-loop escalation.
Risk: Shadowed broker increases load. Mitigation: sample shadowed invocations (default 10%) and backpressure shadowing when staging CPU > 70%.
Risk: Latency of score calc adds tail. Mitigation: compute at edge proxies with TTL and fallback to last-known score.
Risk: Customer confusion when they see 'shed' activity. Mitigation: expose clear Console messaging and allow per-tenant opt-out.
next_steps: Complete PR for mitigation executor and add safe-guarded feature flag: runtime.feature.gsc.enabled
Add Console visualization tile for degradation_score and mitigation history
Coordinate with Privacy to add identifier-stripping middleware for shadow paths
Schedule canary on 2026-03-18 for internal tenants
